article_blocks.text: Strain Type: 80% Indica / 20% Sativa
Genetics: ( Warlock × AK-47 ) × Sensi Star
Breeder: Delta 9 Labs
THC Content: 16–17%
CBD Content: Low
Terpene Profile: N/A
Primary Flavors: Peppermint, pine, earth, wood
Flowering Time (Indoor): 60–70 days
Outdoor Harvest Time: October
Indoor Yield: 300–500 g/m²
Outdoor Yield: Moderate
Grow Difficulty: Easy to moderate

Stargazer —officially styled Star Gazer by Delta 9 Labs—is a compact marijuana hybrid assembled from three strains that earned lasting reputations during the development of modern indoor cannabis: Warlock, AK-47, and Sensi Star. Its character is almost the opposite of what its celestial name might imply. Rather than growing skyward, the plant remains short, thick, and exceptionally bushy, putting its energy into dense foliage and compact flower production.

The effect carries more contrast: physical relaxation arrives alongside enough mental alertness to keep the experience engaging rather than immediately sleepy. Add a woody pine flavor that develops into an unexpectedly cool peppermint finish, and Stargazer becomes an unusual old-school hybrid with an identity that has little in common with today’s candy-heavy weed market. Delta 9 Labs currently lists the cultivar at 80% indica, 20% sativa, with roughly 16–17% THC and a 60–70-day flowering period.
Genetics and Lineage

Delta 9 Labs gives the parentage as Warlock, AK-47, and Sensi Star, describing the genetic contribution as approximately 40% Warlock, 20% AK-47, and 40% Sensi Star. The breeder’s account provides more detail about how that combination was created. A selected Warlock female was first combined with AK-47 genetics, after which the preferred offspring was crossed with a Sensi Star male. The resulting cultivar was stabilized into the compact, indica-heavy Star Gazer maintained by Delta 9 Labs.

Each parent contributes something recognizable. Warlock brings indica structure, resin, sweetness, and a mentally engaging high, while AK-47 contributes vigor and a more animated cerebral dimension. Sensi Star reinforces compact growth and physical potency. Rather than producing an entirely sedating hybrid, those influences balance one another: Stargazer stays short like an indica yet retains more perceptual clarity than its 80% indica classification might lead someone to expect.

The age of the parental stock is also noteworthy. Delta 9 Labs states that the Warlock and AK-47 material used in the project came from older seed stock available roughly a decade before the cross was made, and the breeder specifically valued its connection with the original expressions of those cultivars. That background helps explain why Stargazer feels stylistically closer to classic hashy, pine-dominant cannabis than to the fruit-candy hybrids that dominate many modern dispensary menus.
Effects and Experience

The first portion of the high is more mentally awake than physically heavy. Attention can become slightly sharper, mood improves, and ordinary surroundings may seem more interesting without producing the frantic quality associated with particularly energetic sativas. Delta 9 Labs describes the effect simply as relaxed and good-humored while also noting that the strain can produce a surprisingly strong high for its measured THC range.

Over time, Sensi Star and Warlock ancestry becomes more apparent in the body. Muscular tension begins to loosen, physical activity becomes less compelling, and the initial alertness settles into comfortable calm. The effect can therefore work well for music, a movie, conversation, sitting outside, or other activities where the consumer wants to remain aware without feeling driven to accomplish anything. It is easy to understand why the breeder associated the experience with spending a summer evening looking at the stars.

The reported 16–17% THC level may look modest beside contemporary marijuana regularly marketed above 25%, but THC percentage alone does not determine subjective strength. Delta 9 Labs specifically characterizes the high as strong, suggesting that consumers should not automatically interpret the numerical range as mild. Dose, individual tolerance, harvest maturity, and the chemistry of the actual flower can all change the experience considerably.
Medical Benefits

For medical cannabis consumers, Stargazer’s combination of mental composure and physical relaxation may be more attractive than either an intensely stimulating sativa or an overwhelmingly sedating indica. Some people prefer this kind of effect when dealing with temporary stress, physical tension, low mood, or the difficulty of mentally disengaging at the end of the day. Its comparatively moderate breeder-reported THC range may also appeal to consumers who no longer seek the highest-potency weed available.

There is no cultivar-specific clinical research establishing Stargazer as a treatment for chronic pain, anxiety, depression, insomnia, or another diagnosed condition. Strain names do not provide a reliable substitute for cannabinoid testing, medical guidance, or an individual’s previous response to THC.

Because CBD content is not standardized by the breeder, this should primarily be viewed as THC-oriented cannabis rather than a confirmed balanced THC/CBD medical cultivar. Anyone particularly sensitive to THC-related anxiety, dizziness, or cognitive impairment should begin with a conservative amount even though its traditional reputation emphasizes relaxation.
Flavor Profile and Aroma

Stargazer’s flavor is one of its clearest departures from modern breeding trends. Delta 9 Labs identifies peppermint, pine, and earth as the principal sensory characteristics. Freshly broken flower can initially seem woody and forest-like, with dry earth and resinous pine forming the base. The cooling mint character becomes more noticeable after inhalation, producing an unusual finish that the breeder has compared with peppermint candy.

The smoke moves through several stages rather than delivering one dominant flavor. Natural wood and pine appear early, followed by deeper soil and herbal notes. Peppermint develops toward the end and can remain on the palate after exhalation. That transition gives the weed a clean, almost refreshing finish despite the heavier earthy foundation.

Delta 9 Labs does not publish a laboratory terpene assay for the cultivar, so assigning a definitive dominant terpene would be speculative. Pine aromas are often connected with pinene, while earthy, herbal, and mint-like impressions can arise from several different aromatic compounds working together. The documented pine-earth-peppermint profile is therefore a more reliable reference than any unsupported claim about exact terpene percentages.
Growing Information

Space efficiency is one of Stargazer’s strongest horticultural qualities. Delta 9 Labs describes it as the shortest and bushiest strain in its lineup, with mature flowering plants reaching roughly one meter depending on container volume, airflow, and overall growing conditions. Short, thick leaves create a dense canopy, and the flowers can develop distinctive pink pistils associated with the AK-47 and Warlock side of the family.

Indoor flowering takes approximately 60–70 days, with breeder yields of roughly 300–500 g/m². The plant reportedly prefers soil and coco over rockwool, although Delta 9 Labs notes that it also performs well with automated feeding systems and can develop into a substantial bush. Because lateral growth is strong, selective pruning or low-stress training can help open the center of the canopy and distribute light across more flower sites. Good airflow is particularly important when a naturally compact marijuana plant is allowed to become extremely dense.

The current breeder lists Stargazer as suitable for indoor, outdoor, and greenhouse cultivation, but does not provide a standardized outdoor harvest date or yield figure. Outdoor performance will therefore depend heavily on latitude, planting date, container or root-zone size, and seasonal temperatures. Growers working from breeder information should avoid treating unsupported third-party outdoor numbers as guaranteed traits.
FAQ
Is Stargazer an indica or sativa?

Delta 9 Labs classifies Star Gazer as approximately 80% indica and 20% sativa. Its short stature and bushy architecture strongly reflect the indica side, while the high retains a noticeable cerebral and alert component.
What are the genetics of Stargazer?

The Delta 9 Labs version comes from Warlock, AK-47, and Sensi Star. The breeding process involved Warlock and AK-47 genetics followed by selection and a cross to Sensi Star, producing the final indica-dominant cultivar.
How much THC does Stargazer have?

Delta 9 Labs reports THC around 16–17%. Individual plants and commercial batches may test differently because environment, phenotype, lighting, harvest maturity, and laboratory methodology all affect cannabinoid measurements.
What does Stargazer taste like?
Pine, earth, wood, and peppermint define the traditional flavor. The smoke typically starts woody and natural before moving toward a cool mint-like finish.
How long does Stargazer take to flower?
Indoor flowering takes approximately 60–70 days. Delta 9 Labs lists production around 300–500 g/m² and notes that the plant generally remains close to one meter tall at full flower.
Final Thoughts on Stargazer

Stargazer represents an older approach to cannabis hybridization in which recognizable effect, practical plant structure, and distinctive flavor mattered more than chasing maximum THC. Warlock, AK-47, and Sensi Star give the cultivar a formidable genetic foundation, yet the finished plant is surprisingly manageable: short, bushy, moderately fast to flower, and capable of respectable indoor production.

Its personality becomes clearest after harvest. Woody pine and earth turn toward peppermint on the finish, while the high moves between alert mental relaxation and a comfortable indica body effect. Those characteristics give Stargazer something increasingly valuable in a crowded marijuana market—a profile that is easy to distinguish from dozens of sweeter modern hybrids. For enthusiasts interested in classic breeding genetics or growers looking for a compact weed strain with a strong but relatively composed experience, the Delta 9 Labs cultivar remains an intriguing piece of cannabis breeding history.
